items.heading: Starting Late Is a Bigger
items.text: Starting late is a bigger risk than starting imperfectly. If you are still finishing exams or a final project, you do not need a finished plan - you need to start the first lane now and add the rest as time frees up.

items.heading: Every Graduate Job Search
items.text: Every graduate job search in India runs through some mix of four channels. They are not equally good, and they are not mutually exclusive - the strongest job searches run more than one at the same time.

items.heading: Applying to Hundreds of Roles
items.text: Applying to hundreds of roles with one unchanged resume. A generic resume clears fewer automated filters than a resume tailored to the specific role's listed skills. Volume without targeting mostly produces a long list of silence, not a faster offer.

items.heading: Treating Campus Placements As
items.text: Treating campus placements as the only plan. If your college is not visited by many recruiters, or your branch and CGPA sit outside the usual cutoff, campus alone is a thin plan. Off-campus portals and referrals do not wait for a placement calendar.

items.heading: Waiting to "Feel Ready" Before
items.text: Waiting to "feel ready" before reaching out for a referral. Most people underrate how willing a stranger-adjacent contact is to forward a resume when the ask is small and the message is specific. Waiting for total confidence usually just delays the highest-value channel available to you.

items.heading: Ignoring the National Career Service
items.text: Ignoring the National Career Service and other government listings. Free, real openings exist on the government-run National Career Service portal alongside apprenticeship listings, and most graduates never check it because it is not the platform their friends talk about.
